status: draft, checked against cited sources, awaiting review (2026-10-08)
rules: Explain what the question asks and how the Agency uses the answer. Never suggest which answer to give or predict the outcome: the assessment is the caseworker's professional judgement (decision-flow document, comments c3, c5, c7).
Every statement is grounded in a FAQ record (cited by id) or the decision-flow document. Anything without a source is listed under flags, not written into the text.
related lists FAQ ids whose canonical question the help card shows; clicking one runs it through the normal DCR search.

Form0:Email.description: The email address used to contact you about this application. Use a fictional address in this demo. In a real application, keep the receipt and any reference number you get after sending.

Form0:Phone.description: A phone number for questions about your application, including the country code. Use a fictional number in this demo.
flags: No source describes how the Agency uses the phone number; text kept to the demo instruction.

Form0:A1_1.description: The month you want the supplement to start from. If it is granted, it is paid from the month you applied for, but never earlier than the month the Agency received your application through minSU. It is only paid for months in which you receive an SU stipend or a final loan.

Form0:A2.description: Select every type of impairment you want the Agency to consider. The Agency only assesses the impairments you name as the basis of your application, even if others are mentioned in your records, and you need documentation for each one. The type you choose does not decide the outcome: the assessment looks at whether the impairment is permanent, how severe it is, and how it limits paid work.

options.Impaired: Physical impairment, for example severe muscle or nerve conditions, severe spinal conditions or cerebral palsy.
options.Neurological: An impairment of the brain or nervous system.
options.Mental: A mental impairment, for example severe difficulties due to personality disorder, eating disorder, OCD or anxiety; schizophrenia-spectrum disorders; bipolar disorder or recurrent depression; ADHD or autism spectrum disorder.
options.Other: An impairment that fits none of the types above. The examples are not a complete list, and other conditions can also qualify.

Form0:A2.option_note: Having one of the example conditions does not by itself guarantee approval.
flags: Option labels in the graph are 'item 1' to 'item 6' (values Impaired, Neurological, Visual, Hearing, Mental, Other); the form likely shows the placeholders. Proposed labels: Physical, Neurological, Visual, Hearing, Mental, Other. Values unchanged, so routing is unaffected.
'Neurological' has no source definition; FAQ_08 lists MS and severe nerve conditions under physical impairments, so the two options overlap. Text kept generic.

Form0:Impairment_type.description: Whether the impairment has been present since birth, or arose later through an illness or an accident. For a congenital impairment, recent records describing your current functional level are often missing, so it is especially important to submit your medical history and your most recent records. You can also use your personal statement to describe your situation.

options.1: Present from birth, for example cerebral palsy, muscular dystrophy, intellectual disability, autism spectrum disorder, congenital blindness or severe visual impairment, or deafness.
options.2: Arose later in life, through an illness or an accident. You will then be asked whether it is permanent.

Form0:Impairment_definition.description: Whether the impairment was permanent by its nature from the moment it first appeared. Permanent means it is not expected to improve substantially, on its own or with treatment, within a longer number of years. The Agency makes this assessment from your medical records; answer as well as you can.

options.1: It was permanent by its nature from the start.
options.2: It was not permanent from the start. A condition like this can still be regarded as permanent once it has lasted around a year. You will be asked how long it has lasted.
options.3: You cannot tell. You will be asked how long it has lasted.

Form0:A14.description: Whether you have had the symptoms or effects for at least about a year. A condition that is not permanent by definition can be regarded as permanent once it has lasted around a year. This is an assessment guideline, not an automatic threshold: a shorter or longer period can also be relevant depending on the evidence.

options.true: You have had symptoms or effects for a year or more.
options.false: You have had them for less than a year.

Form0:Time_limited.description: Whether you currently receive a time-limited handicaptillæg. A time-limited award is given when it has been made probable, but not finally established, that the impairment is permanent. It runs until a date stated in the decision letter.

options.true: You have a current time-limited award. You will be asked when it ends.
options.false: You do not currently receive a time-limited award.

Form0:A17.description: Whether your current time-limited award ends within three months. An extension is applied for through minSU before the award expires, but no earlier than three months before it expires, with medical documentation newer than what the Agency already has.

options.true: Your current award ends within the next three months.
options.false: It ends more than three months from now.

flags: The form does not say what happens when the award ends later than three months from now. FAQ_37 implies an extension cannot be applied for yet; the help text does not state this, pending your decision.

Form0:Prev_work.description: Whether you had paid work in the last three years. Work both before and after your application can be part of the Agency’s overall assessment, and the Agency also receives information on your working hours and income from the Danish Tax Agency. It is one part of an overall assessment.

options.true: You had paid work at some point in this period. You will be asked about the hours.
options.false: You had no paid work in this period.

flags: The three-year period comes from the form; no source states it.

Form0:A15.description: The average number of hours a week you worked in that job. Give your best estimate. The Agency also receives your working hours and income from the Danish Tax Agency.
flags: No source says how to answer with more than one job. Not addressed in the text.

Form0:Plan_work_studies.description: Whether you plan to take paid work alongside your studies. The supplement is for students whose impairment very significantly limits their ability to take paid work while studying, so planned work is part of the assessment.

options.true: You plan paid work of any amount. You will be asked how many hours.
options.false: You do not plan paid work alongside your studies.

Form0:A16.description: How many hours a week you plan to work alongside your studies. Planned work is part of the work-capacity assessment. If you receive the supplement, your income allowance (fribeløb) is reduced.
flags: Deliberately does not quote the 5-6 hours indicator from FAQ_16 in the field text, so the help does not read as advice on what to enter. The linked FAQ shows it.

Form0:Samtykke.description: Confirms that you will use fictional information in this demonstration. Choosing No ends the demo without sending anything.

options.true: Continue the demo with fictional information.
options.false: Stop the demo. Nothing is sent.

flags: The event id 'Samtykke' (consent) suggests the real form's consent question, which may mean something else (for example consent for the Agency to obtain information). The text describes the demo question only.

Form0:A5.description: A personal statement describing how the impairment affects your daily life, ability to work, treatment and education. It supplements your medical records but does not replace them, and it is not part of the minimum documentation requirement. For a congenital impairment it is a good place to describe your current situation. Demo: only a filename is recorded; file contents are not uploaded.

Form0:A11.description: As a minimum, records from your GP, a specialist doctor, a hospital or an outpatient clinic that describe the permanent impairment you are applying on and are current for it. A statement that only confirms a diagnosis, a medication list, or a decision without medical information is not enough on its own. You may cross out sensitive details that are not about the impairment, treatment or ability to work. Demo: only a filename is recorded; file contents are not uploaded.
flags: Four related FAQs; the card limit was 1-3. Drop FAQ_P06 or FAQ_P04 if you want three.

Form0:A10.description: Check your answers before sending. In this demo nothing is sent to an authority. In a real application you should receive a receipt after sending, and processing time varies.
